newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index eases in sellers market.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index eases in sellers market.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index shed a further 4.30 points to close at 3373.57 on Tuesday as investors continued offloading key shares, bourse officials said.
Turnover was posted at 22.295 million shillings on 407,566 shares compared to 15.880 million shillings on 424,834 shares on Monday.
"The price madness that was seen on the index linked shares at the beginning of this year was not sustainable, as it was driven by speculators," a senior dealer said.
Barclays Bank lost six shillings to close at 100, while Standard Chartered Bank eased to 46.75 from 47.
Kenya Airways closed at 8.45 from 8.60 while Uchumi Supermarket traded at 36 from 36.25.
"You've got to remember the Kenyan market is dividend and bonus driven and investors were willing to buy shares at unreasonable levels in the hope that they'd make good gains," another broker said.
"Now that results are out, many of these speculators are getting out of the market," he added.
Foreign interest in Kenya Commercial Bank prevailed. Foreign investors bought 1,400 shares between 94-96 from 94.
Brokers said they expected the prevailing bearish sentiment in the market to persist until mid-year when buying interest is expected to pick up on interim results.
In the agriculturals, Rea Vipingo Plantations traded 48,100 shares at 9.0 from 9.50.
